column1: The Listening Book|1991|0|0||7,4,5,5,7,9,2,8,8,8|W. A. Mathieu|Short essays distinguish kinds of attention and overlooked features of sound. Sensory observation supplies modest transferable habits, but little integration with institutions, technology or strategic constraints.

Playful Parenting|2001|0|0||7,4,5,5,7,8,1,8,8,7|Lawrence J. Cohen|Play is used to explain communication, trust and emotional expression in children. Examples add interpersonal applications; clinical experience is not equivalent to controlled causal validation.

Advice on Upskilling|2025|0|0||6,5,7,5,7,7,4,6,7,6|Justin Skycak|Collected essays discuss practice, consistency and skill development across domains. The author identifies the public PDF as a developing book; its general learning advice is not a specialist technical curriculum. https://www.justinmath.com/advice-on-upskilling/

The Icarus Deception|2012|0|0||5,5,5,4,5,7,3,6,8,6|Seth Godin|Contrasts creative initiative with industrial conformity. The distinction can guide choices, but broad exhortation and selected examples add less evidence and mechanism than the ambitious framing suggests.

So Good They Can’t Ignore You|2012|0|0||6,6,7,6,7,8,4,7,8,7|Cal Newport|Skill accumulation, bargaining power and career autonomy form a useful alternative to searching for a pre-existing passion. Selected career cases support hypotheses more than universal causal claims.

Practicing Mind|2006|0|10||5,3,5,3,6,8,1,5,7,6|Thomas M. Sterner|Separates attention to the process from attachment to outcomes. A durable practice heuristic remains, but the central personal philosophy has limited systems depth and repeated motivational application.

Drive|2009|0|0||6,6,7,6,7,8,4,6,8,7|Daniel H. Pink|Autonomy, mastery and purpose organize a comparison of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. Task and incentive conditions matter; examples do not justify treating monetary rewards as uniformly harmful.

Discover Your Inner Economist|2007|0|0||7,6,8,6,8,8,4,9,8,8|Tyler Cowen|Applies incentives, signaling and opportunity costs to varied ordinary choices. Different applications add useful constraints, though some advice is personal interpretation rather than tested economic inference.

Ignore Everybody|2009|0|0||5,3,5,3,6,8,2,5,8,6|Hugh MacLeod|Short observations on independence, incentives and creative work offer portable reminders. Anecdotal authority and limited causal development keep the score low despite concise presentation.

Tribes|2008|0|0||5,6,6,4,5,6,3,6,8,6|Seth Godin|Explains group formation around shared ideas and leadership. A few transferable coordination ideas survive dated online examples, but inspirational framing and weak boundary conditions limit depth.

Nineteen Ways of Looking at Consciousness|2022|0|10||7,5,5,6,7,8,4,8,8,8|Patrick House|Multiple interpretations of one neurological episode expose the gap between observations and explanations of experience. The philosophical variations add distinctions but no settled causal synthesis.

Cosmopolitanism|2006|0|10||8,6,7,6,8,9,3,9,8,9|Kwame Anthony Appiah|Distinguishes universal concern from agreement about values and ways of life. Cases clarify pluralism and cross-cultural cooperation; normative argument, not empirical systems engineering, is central.

Battleground: 10 Conflicts that Explain the New Middle East|2024|0|10|2023|8,8,7,7,8,7,7,9,8,8|Christopher Phillips|Compares regional conflicts through state interests, alliances and external intervention. Cross-case links add strategic knowledge; recent events and unresolved outcomes reduce durability confidence.

Heirs to Forgotten Kingdoms: the Disappearing Religions of the Middle East|2014|10|0||8,6,5,5,8,8,2,8,9,8|Gerard Russell|Field reporting connects minority religious communities with historical institutions and cultural persistence. Distinct traditions add knowledge, but minority issues dominate and direct strategic transfer is limited.

Wish Lanterns / China’s New Youth|2016|10|0|2016|8,6,4,5,7,8,2,7,9,8|Alec Ash|Six lives connect work, family aspirations and rapid social change. The comparisons add context beyond individual biography, with low technical fit and a country-centered historical narrative.

Hold On to Your Kids|2004|0|0||6,4,5,5,6,7,1,8,8,7|Gordon Neufeld; Gabor Maté|Attachment explains tensions between parental guidance and peer influence. The central model offers interpersonal lessons, but broad cultural and developmental claims require stronger causal support.

The Stoic Challenge|2019|0|10||6,4,5,4,6,8,1,7,8,7|William B. Irvine|Reframes setbacks as tests of attention and response. The philosophical heuristic is reusable; extended personal application supplies modest additional learning and little systems integration.

Useful Delusions|2021|0|0||6,6,6,6,7,8,3,7,8,7|Shankar Vedantam; Bill Mesler|Compares cases in which inaccurate beliefs appear to improve well-being or coordination. Benefits and costs need separate causal tests; useful examples do not establish that self-deception is generally advantageous.

Nietzsche: a complete introduction|2002|0|10||7,4,5,5,7,9,1,8,8,7|Roy Jackson|Explains major concepts and arguments in Nietzsche's philosophy. An expository survey rather than an advocacy of extremism; specialist novelty and direct technical fit are low.

What Everyone Needs to Know about Islam|2002|0|0||8,6,5,5,7,8,3,9,8,8|John L. Esposito|A descriptive question-and-answer survey distinguishes beliefs, practices and historical institutions. It explains religion rather than requiring doctrinal assent; breadth is stronger than causal depth.

Almost Perfect|2021|0|0||5,3,4,3,5,7,1,6,8,6|Erika Lemay|A performance memoir describes discipline, preparation and ambition. Some practice heuristics transfer, but personal success cannot establish general causal rules and athletic artistry has low domain fit.

The Courage to Be Happy|2016|0|10||5,4,5,4,6,7,1,6,6,6|Ichiro Kishimi; Fumitake Koga|An expository dialogue presents Adlerian ideas about education, agency and relationships. The dialogue is philosophical instruction rather than a novel; recurring objections and broad psychological claims limit density and evidence.

Essays and Aphorisms|1851|0|10||6,4,5,5,7,9,1,10,8,8|Arthur Schopenhauer|Selected philosophical essays offer distinctions about judgment, suffering and conduct. Unsupported generalizations, including views about women, lower evidential assessment; intellectual influence does not establish truth. Original essays date to Parerga and Paralipomena, not the modern English selection.

Wanting|2021|0|10||6,6,6,5,6,8,3,6,8,7|Luke Burgis|Mimetic desire supplies a lens on competition and goals. Different examples offer applications, but the interpretive framework is broader than its causal evidence and the source reports an unclear practical conclusion.

The Art of Creative Thinking|2015|0|0||5,4,5,3,6,7,2,6,8,6|Rod Judkins|Brief creative examples supply prompts for changing perspective. Varied cases add some learning, but selected success anecdotes offer limited mechanisms and evidential control.

Will|2021|10|0|2020|6,4,4,3,6,7,1,5,9,7|Will Smith; Mark Manson|A celebrity memoir distills ambition and family experience into personal lessons. Narration is stronger than causal explanation; transferable reflections prevent an automatic no-payload veto, while the celebrity focus triggers T11.

The Alter Ego Effect|2019|0|0||5,3,5,3,5,6,1,5,8,6|Todd Herman|Role-based reframing can help separate action from anxiety. Performance anecdotes and the organizing metaphor provide limited causal evidence and a relatively small payload.

The Consolations of Philosophy|2000|0|10||7,5,6,5,7,9,1,6,9,8|Alain de Botton|Philosophical lives and arguments illuminate frustration, status and ordinary problems. Distinct thinkers add perspectives, but selective interpretation and personal advice limit systems depth.

Perennial Seller|2017|0|0||6,6,7,5,7,8,3,6,8,7|Ryan Holiday|Connects durable creative products with audience development and distribution. Commercial cases offer transferable constraints; successful examples do not isolate the causes of longevity.

Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise|2016|0|0||7,6,8,7,8,9,5,9,8,8|Anders Ericsson; Robert Pool|Deliberate practice, feedback and mental representations explain aspects of expertise. Skill comparisons add boundary conditions; practice is not the sole cause of every performance difference.

The Truth|2015|0|0||6,3,4,3,5,7,1,5,8,6|Neil Strauss|A relationship memoir contrasts recurring behavior with changed commitments. Reflections offer some generalizable distinctions but personal detail dominates much of the reading.

Geography of Time|1997|0|0||8,6,6,6,8,8,3,8,8,8|Robert Levine|Cross-cultural observations compare pace, punctuality and social time. Distinct cases improve understanding of coordination, while descriptive comparisons limit causal certainty.

Show Your Work|2014|0|0||6,4,6,4,7,7,3,6,8,7|Austin Kleon|Sharing process, feedback and participation supplies a useful model of creative visibility. Short examples add practical distinctions; online context is more perishable than the core communication ideas.

Choose Yourself!|2013|0|0||4,4,5,3,5,5,2,4,8,5|James Altucher|Personal experiences encourage agency and independent work. Selected anecdotes and sweeping prescriptions limit evidence and mechanism, while a modest transferable initiative heuristic remains.

Why Smart People Make Big Money Mistakes|1999|0|10||7,6,7,7,8,8,4,8,8,7|Gary Belsky; Thomas Gilovich|Financial examples distinguish sunk costs, loss aversion and mental accounting. Cases add useful decision constraints; finance is central and behavioral effects depend on context.

Management of the Absurd|1996|0|0||6,6,7,5,7,8,4,7,8,7|Richard Farson|Organizational paradoxes challenge simple prescriptions about control and communication. Contrasting situations provide transfer, though aphoristic conclusions have limited causal validation.

CrowdSourcing|2008|0|0||7,8,8,7,7,7,7,7,8,7|Jeff Howe|Distributed contributions connect incentives, platform design and coordination. Varied cases reveal useful conditions, while early internet enthusiasm and success selection lower durability and evidence.

Wikinomics|2006|0|0||6,8,7,6,7,6,7,7,8,7|Don Tapscott; Anthony D. Williams|Mass collaboration links digital infrastructure, incentives and organizational boundaries. Comparative examples carry useful mechanisms, but broad revolutionary language and dated cases weaken generality.

Meatball Sundae|2007|0|10||6,6,6,5,6,6,4,6,8,6|Seth Godin|Argues that communication tools require compatible products and business models. Marketing is the center; changing platforms date some examples, while organizational fit is the durable principle.

On Looking: Eleven Walks with Expert Eyes|2013|0|0||8,5,6,5,8,9,2,8,9,8|Alexandra Horowitz|Experts notice different features of the same surroundings, exposing selective attention. Each walk adds a different distinction; observational inquiry rather than urban history is central.

Islam Explained|2020|0|0||7,4,4,4,7,8,1,6,8,7|Ahmad Rashid Salim|A short explanatory introduction outlines Islamic beliefs and practices. Description of doctrine is not itself doctrinal advocacy; limited depth and technical relevance keep the score low.

New China Playbook|2023|10|10||7,9,8,8,8,7,7,9,8,7|Keyu Jin|Connects Chinese finance, firms, households and government incentives. Insider interpretation supplies useful mechanisms but needs counterevidence; the national and financial-policy center triggers both thematic deductions.

Political Thought of Xi Jinping|2024|10|10||8,7,6,7,8,8,5,9,7,8|Steve Tsang; Olivia Cheung|Analyzes stated and implied governing ideas and their institutional effects. Studying a leader's ideology is distinct from recruiting allegiance to it; national political leadership triggers both thematic deductions.

Excellent Advice for Living|2023|0|0||5,3,5,3,6,8,2,6,8,7|Kevin Kelly|Brief maxims offer decision prompts across ordinary life. Variety prevents pure repetition, but unsupported compression and little explanation limit evidence and causal depth.

Japanese Mind|2002|10|0||7,6,5,5,7,8,2,7,7,7|Roger J. Davies; Osamu Ikeno|Explains cultural concepts through everyday practices and historical context. Useful comparisons risk treating a diverse society as uniform; Japanese national-cultural scope triggers T11.

Surviving AI|2015|0|0||6,7,6,6,7,6,7,6,8,7|Calum Chace|Surveys AI development, disruption and possible long-run risks. Speculative extrapolation is not an automatic veto, but dated frontier assumptions and introductory depth limit confidence and durability.

Die Empty|2013|0|0||5,4,5,3,5,7,2,5,8,6|Todd Henry|Distinguishes planning, producing and connecting ideas. The work categories provide a modest reusable heuristic; motivational reinforcement supplies less distinct learning than the framing suggests.

Getting the Love You Want|1988|0|0||5,4,4,4,6,7,1,7,8,6|Harville Hendrix|Interprets relationship patterns through early attachments and unmet needs. Clinical examples offer reflection, while broad developmental explanations and treatment claims have limited demonstrated causal support here.

Making Ideas Happen|2010|0|0||6,6,7,6,7,8,5,7,8,7|Scott Belsky|Connects creative work with execution routines, collaboration and accountability. Concrete organizational constraints transfer, but selected practitioner stories limit causal confidence.

Ikigai|2011|0|10||5,5,5,4,6,7,3,4,7,6|Sebastian Marshall|Essays combine agency, negotiation, skill building and historical examples. This is Marshall's collection, not the García/Miralles book; broad personal philosophy provides limited coherent evidence.

You Are Not So Smart|2011|0|0||6,5,6,5,8,7,3,6,8,7|David McRaney|A collection of cognitive-bias explanations offers useful distinctions with high topic variety. Findings vary in robustness and many examples require more context than the compact presentation provides.

Business Stripped Bare|2008|0|0||6,7,7,6,7,8,5,8,8,7|Richard Branson|Virgin business stories connect branding, people, risk and organizational choices. Firsthand access supplies useful decisions, but self-presentation and success selection constrain evidence.
